title: ORM Data Model Leakage (Value Objects as Tables)
pattern: Mapping local Value Objects (attributes with no conceptual identity of their own) to distinct database tables with surrogate primary keys rather than denormalizing them into the parent entity's table.
why_bad: It forces unnecessary database normalization, table joins, and surrogate identity keys onto conceptually immutable value objects, leaking relational database constraints into the logical domain model.
detection: Entity-relationship mapping where a type without a unique business identity (e.g., coordinates, address) is declared as a separate relation with its own auto-incremented surrogate key.
counterexample: The value object is shared globally as a reference data table (e.g., standard postal codes list).
fix: Embed the value object's attributes directly into the parent table's columns (denormalization) using ORM Embedded/Value patterns.
